full_judgment: 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit No.91 of 1994 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal against the present opposite-party Nos. 1-3/11-20 and one Chand Baru bibi, the predecessor opposite party Nos. 4-10 for declaration of title in the land described in schedule "ka" of the plaint and for declaration that the auction sale mentioned in schedule "Kha" of the plaint is collusive, fraudulent and false with a further declaration that the V.P. proceedings described in schedule "Ga" of the plaint is illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff contending inter-alia that the suit property originally belonged to one Jogendra Nath who purchased the same in the benami of one Mathura Nath and Sukumar out of his own money. The R.S. record was prepared in the name of Mathura Nath. Subsiquently, Jogendra Nath executed a will in favour of one Shachindra Nath in the year 1356 B.S. and thereafter Jogendra Nath died on 14.04.1960 A.D. Shachindra Nath filed a Probate case being No.32 of 1960 in which Probate was granted on 11.01.1962. Subsequently while Mathura Nath and Sukumar challenged the execution of will and also denied to execute a deed of nadabi in favour of Shachindra Nath a Title Suit being No. 97/98 of 1963 was filed by Shachindra Nath. That suit was decreed in favour of Shachindra. Thereafter Shachindra mutated his name in S.A. khatian No. 210. Shachindra Nath transferred the suit property in favour of the defendant Nos.9-11 who sold out the same in favour of the plaintiff on 25.02.1964. Subsequently the plaintiff mutated his name and paid rent to the Government. The plaintiff came to know that the suit land was auction sold in favour of the defendant Nos.1-5 on 29.05.1955 in a Rent Suit No. 91 of 1954 and by virtue of a Execution Case No. 339 of 1955 auction purchasers mutated their names in the S.A. khatian for the suit land. The Rent Suit was false, collusive and created. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the original owner of the land was all along a citizen of this country and he never migrated to India and as such the suit land cannot be a vested property. The plaintiff in the 1st part of Chaitra, 1396 B.S. came to learn about the vested property proceeding as well as the auction purchase of the defendant Nos.1-5 and thereafter he filed the original suit against the defendants.
